Getting Started

Who the mentorship is for

Start here if you are deciding whether your background, location, experience, or current schedule is a good fit for Anderseed.

Is the mentorship suitable for complete beginners with no IT experience?
Yes. The mentorship is designed to take beginners from foundational Business Analysis concepts into guided project work, portfolio artefacts, career positioning, and interview preparation. You do not need previous IT employment, although you must be willing to practise, complete tasks, and act on feedback.
Who is the Anderseed Business Analysis mentorship for?
It is for adult learners, including complete beginners, career changers, graduates, people returning to work, professionals with transferable skills, and aspiring Business Analysts who want more practical structure and accountability. It is also suitable for learners who understand some theory but do not yet feel able to demonstrate Business Analysis work confidently.
Can I join from outside the UK?
Yes. The mentorship is open to adult learners worldwide. The projects, terminology, documentation standards, recruitment guidance, and professional expectations use UK-style Business Analysis industry practice, while the underlying skills and artefacts are transferable to many international markets.
Do I need a degree, certification, or previous Business Analysis role?
No specific degree, certification, or previous Business Analyst job is required. The programme starts with the fundamentals and helps you connect existing education, work, volunteering, or life experience to Business Analysis skills. Any employer or professional certification requirements remain separate from the mentorship.
Can I join while working full time or managing other commitments?
Yes. The programme is designed to work around different schedules, and teaching sessions are recorded for enrolled learners. You will still need regular time for project tasks, feedback, portfolio work, and career preparation, but the amount can be adjusted around your responsibilities and chosen pace.
Can I use the free BA assessment before deciding about premium mentorship?
Yes. The free BA Readiness Assessment is a sensible starting point if you want to understand your current stage, recognise your strongest area and identify the growth priority that can move you forward before paying for guided support. You can also join the free Telegram community, read the blog, and return to the mentorship when the timing is right.
Programme Delivery

How the mentorship works

The programme combines live teaching, recordings, practical work, feedback, career preparation, and a small collaborative cohort.

What is included in the 8-week Business Analysis mentorship?
The programme includes live mentor-led training, recorded sessions, guided project practice, a professional BA portfolio, CV and LinkedIn support, a job application guide, mock interviews, career coaching, recruiter outreach guidance, community access, and support after the live cohort. The pricing section lists the current bundle inclusions.
Is this a course or a mentorship programme?
It is a structured mentorship programme rather than a self-paced video course. You receive teaching, guided practice, mentor feedback, accountability, project review, and career support so that you can apply what you learn instead of only watching lessons.
Why is the live cohort eight weeks if the website shows a 90-day journey?
The core mentor-led cohort runs for eight weeks. The 90-day journey describes the wider development path, including onboarding, live training, project completion, portfolio refinement, and job-readiness activity. It is a planning framework and not a promise that every learner will reach the same outcome on the same date.
Are the live sessions recorded?
Yes. Teaching sessions are recorded so enrolled learners can revisit explanations or catch up when work and personal commitments prevent live attendance. Recordings are for the registered cohort only and are not a substitute for completing the practical work or engaging with feedback.
How long can I access the session recordings?
Enrolled learners can access programme recordings for 12 months, subject to the programme terms and the continued availability of the learning platform. Recordings and programme materials are for personal learning only and must not be copied, shared, resold, or published.
What happens if I miss a live session?
You can use the recording to catch up and continue with the related task. Live attendance is encouraged because it gives you immediate discussion and feedback, but missing an occasional session does not automatically prevent you from continuing. You remain responsible for reviewing the material and completing required work.
How much time should I commit each week?
There is no single weekly number that suits everyone. Your commitment depends on your starting point, work and family responsibilities, project pace, and career goals. Plan for the live or recorded teaching plus regular time for project tasks, portfolio development, CV or LinkedIn work, applications, and feedback.
How large is each cohort?
Cohorts are intentionally kept small to support useful discussion, efficient collaboration, mentor attention, and practical feedback. The exact number may vary by intake, but Anderseed limits places when necessary to protect the quality of the learning experience.
Will I receive a certificate?
Yes. Learners who complete the programme and required project work receive an Anderseed certificate of completion. The certificate confirms participation and completion; it is not a regulated qualification, professional licence, or guarantee of employment.
Projects & Portfolio

The practical work you will build

The mentorship is designed to give learners credible, guided project evidence they can explain clearly in applications and interviews.

What practical experience and portfolio work will I build?
You will work through an end-to-end business case and create artefacts such as stakeholder analysis, a RACI matrix, a power-interest grid, AS-IS and TO-BE process maps, BPMN diagrams, requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, a BRD, and a prototype walkthrough. The emphasis is on understanding why each artefact is needed and being able to explain your decisions.
What types of business cases can I work on?
The flagship experience is one continuous Salesforce CRM implementation, worked through from Discovery to Deployment. You can then apply the same Business Analysis approach more independently in an HCM transformation challenge, with an ERP procurement scenario available as an optional capstone.
Does the project count as real Business Analysis experience?
It provides realistic, guided project experience that helps you practise the work, language, judgement, and deliverables expected from a Business Analyst. It is not the same as paid employment or an undisclosed client role, so you should present it honestly as a mentorship project or portfolio case study while explaining the practical work you completed.
Will the project help me speak more confidently in interviews?
That is one of its main purposes. You will have a structured business problem, stakeholders, evidence, decisions, processes, requirements, and outputs to discuss. Mentor feedback helps you turn the work into a clear interview story without claiming experience you do not have.
Do I need to know how to code?
No. Business Analysis focuses on understanding needs, stakeholders, processes, requirements, value, and change. You may work with business and delivery tools, but software development or programming experience is not a prerequisite for joining.
Will I receive feedback on my project and portfolio?
Yes. Feedback and refinement are central to the mentorship. You will be expected to review comments, improve your artefacts, correct unclear thinking, and practise presenting your work as a Business Analyst rather than submitting a document once and moving on.
Can I use the finished project in my portfolio?
Yes, you can use your own completed work as a portfolio case study and discuss it in applications and interviews. You must protect personal information, respect any confidentiality instructions, credit templates appropriately, and avoid sharing restricted programme materials or other learners' work.
Career Outcomes

Job-readiness and realistic expectations

Anderseed strengthens your skills, evidence, positioning, and support, while being transparent about the parts of hiring no training provider can control.

Does the 90-day journey or six-month support guarantee a job?
No. The journey shown on the website is a realistic happy-path illustration, not a promise that every learner will be hired within 90 days or six months. Employment outcomes depend on your effort, prior experience, location, market conditions, application consistency, interview performance, right-to-work position, and employer decisions.
What does Business Analyst-ready mean?
It means being better prepared to understand BA responsibilities, produce and explain core artefacts, discuss an end-to-end project, present transferable experience, and approach applications and interviews with a clear strategy. It does not mean that learning stops after the programme or that an employer must offer you a role.
Is the career support useful outside the UK?
Yes. Core BA skills, stakeholder thinking, requirements, process analysis, documentation, and interview storytelling are internationally transferable. The programme uses UK-style industry experience and recruitment practice, so learners applying elsewhere should also adapt their CV, terminology, salary expectations, and job-search approach to their local market.
Do you help with CV, LinkedIn, applications, and interviews?
Yes. The mentorship includes CV and LinkedIn frameworks and review, job application guidance, mock interviews, career coaching, and support explaining transferable and project experience clearly. Learners must still implement the feedback and submit their own applications.
What does access to 50+ BA recruiter and hiring contacts mean?
It means access to a curated set of relevant recruiter and hiring contacts plus guidance on professional outreach, networking, follow-up, and positioning. It does not guarantee a personal introduction, response, interview, vacancy, or job offer from any contact.
Does Anderseed apply for jobs or attend interviews for me?
No. Anderseed provides tools, feedback, preparation, and accountability, but you are responsible for searching, networking, applying, responding to recruiters, preparing properly, and attending interviews. This keeps your applications truthful and helps you build the independence needed for a long-term career.
What salary can I expect after the programme?
No salary is guaranteed. Any salary or contract-rate information on the website is an indicative market snapshot and can vary by country, location, industry, role scope, prior experience, market conditions, and employer. Always check current vacancies and local salary sources before making a financial decision.
What support continues after the live cohort?
Learners retain access to the alumni community for ongoing peer support, encouragement, career discussion, and relevant updates. Once you secure a role, Anderseed also provides six months of reasonable workplace guidance, including help thinking through unfamiliar BA tasks and professional situations; it does not replace your employer's training, management, or accountability.
Payments & Refunds

Pricing, payment, cancellation, and changes

Review the current pricing page and terms before paying. The answers below summarise the main arrangements and do not remove your legal rights.

What is included in the programme price?
The programme price covers the bundle shown in the pricing section, including the live cohort, recordings, guided project work, portfolio development, career materials and review, interview preparation, recruiter outreach guidance, post-hire support, and alumni community access. Check the current pricing section before purchase because inclusions and cohort availability may be updated.
Can I buy individual services without joining the full programme?
Yes, where availability is shown. Services such as CV support, LinkedIn review, job application guidance, career counselling, or interview preparation may be purchased separately. The programme bundle is priced to combine training, project work, and career support at a lower total than purchasing all listed services individually.
What payment methods are available?
Before applying, you can review the available Card, Klarna Pay in 3, Clearpay Pay in 4, and bank-transfer options on the checkout page. No payment is taken with the application. If your place is approved, Anderseed sends secure payment instructions so you can choose the method that suits you. Klarna and Clearpay are subject to provider eligibility and terms, and a cohort place is not confirmed until payment or an approved payment arrangement has been verified.
What are the payment, cancellation and refund options?
You can pay by the methods displayed at checkout. For an online purchase, the current terms provide a 14-day cancellation period. If you ask Anderseed to begin providing services during that period and then cancel, a proportionate amount may be retained for services already supplied; after the cancellation period, fees are generally non-refundable except where the law or your statutory rights require otherwise.
What happens if I request a refund after the programme has started?
Your request will be assessed under the terms, the timing of purchase, the services already delivered, and applicable consumer law. After the 14-day cancellation period, programme fees are generally non-refundable. Missing sessions or deciding not to continue does not automatically create a refund because recordings and programme access remain available.
Can I move my place to a future cohort?
One transfer to a future cohort may be allowed when requested before the original programme starts, subject to available places and written confirmation from Anderseed. A transfer is not automatic after teaching or personalised services have begun, and any exceptional request will be considered fairly against the programme terms.
What happens if Anderseed postpones or cancels a cohort?
If Anderseed cancels a cohort and cannot provide a suitable replacement, affected learners can choose a full refund for the undelivered programme or transfer to an available future cohort. If a session is rescheduled, Anderseed will provide reasonable notice and, where possible, a recording or replacement session.
Community & Support

Free community, alumni access, and learner conduct

Anderseed provides different levels of support before, during, and after the premium programme.

What is the difference between the free Telegram community and the alumni community?
The free Telegram community is open to prospective learners and shares BA tips, encouragement, events, and cohort updates. The alumni community is part of the premium programme and is intended for deeper peer connection, continued career discussion, and support after completion.
What does lifetime alumni community access mean?
It means continued access after your cohort for as long as Anderseed operates the community and you follow its rules. The platform, format, schedule, and activities may change over time so the community can remain useful and sustainable.
What behaviour is expected in sessions and community spaces?
Learners must communicate respectfully, protect other people's personal information and work, avoid harassment or discrimination, and use programme resources responsibly. Serious or repeated harmful behaviour may lead to restricted or removed access under the programme terms.
Can I stay connected if I am not ready for premium mentorship?
Yes. You can complete the free BA Readiness Assessment, join the free Telegram community, follow Anderseed content, and read the blog without joining the paid cohort. These resources can help you build clarity until you are ready for structured mentorship.
Privacy & Recordings

How personal information is handled

The FAQ gives a plain-English summary. The dedicated privacy notice explains the applicable purposes, rights, and contact route in more detail.

What personal information does Anderseed collect?
For the BA Readiness Assessment, information includes your eight answers, calculated result, a secure technical identifier and, at the result-delivery step, your first name and email address. A separate optional marketing choice is recorded only when the result form is submitted. Depending on how else you interact with Anderseed, information may also include your phone number, referral source, application details, payment-related records, messages, feedback, and programme participation information.
Why is my personal information used?
Assessment information is used to calculate, store and display the personalised result you requested. Anonymous step events are used to understand the assessment funnel. Other information is used to respond to enquiries, process applications and payments, provide programme access and support, administer recordings and community spaces, meet legal or accounting obligations, improve services, and send marketing only where there is an appropriate lawful basis.
Do I have to appear on camera in recorded sessions?
No. Cameras are optional. Learners are told that teaching sessions are recorded and can keep their camera off or limit personal information shared on screen. Private 1:1 or sensitive conversations should not be included in a group recording unless the people involved have been clearly informed and the recording is appropriate.
Who can view programme recordings?
Recordings are restricted to authorised Anderseed personnel and enrolled learners who need access for the programme. Learners must not download, publish, forward, resell, or share recordings with anyone outside the authorised cohort. Access is normally removed after the stated 12-month period or earlier where required for safety, privacy, or compliance.
Is my information sold or shared with third parties?
Anderseed does not sell personal information. Assessment records use first-party application storage operated through Anderseed's hosting and database infrastructure. Trusted providers may process other information for hosting, forms, payments, analytics, video sessions, recordings, email services, or customer administration. Brevo is not connected to the assessment in this MVP, so assessment contacts are not automatically transferred to it at this stage.
Can I unsubscribe from marketing or exercise my data rights?
Yes. The assessment marketing checkbox is separate and optional: your name and email are requested for the result-delivery step, but leaving the marketing box unticked does not prevent access to your result. If you opt in later, you can unsubscribe or withdraw consent at any time. Subject to applicable law, you may also request access, correction, deletion, restriction, or objection relating to your personal information.
How long is my information kept?
An unfinished assessment draft is kept in your browser for up to 24 hours. Anonymous raw funnel events are kept for up to 7 days before deletion after aggregation. A named assessment lead, including the contact and recorded marketing choice, is initially kept for up to 12 months and then reviewed for deletion, anonymisation, or a documented continuing need. Programme recordings are normally available to enrolled learners for 12 months; the privacy notice explains other records.
Help & Accessibility

Questions, adjustments, and concerns

Contact Anderseed early if you need clarification or reasonable support to take part effectively.

Can I request an accessibility adjustment?
Yes. Contact Anderseed before enrolment or as soon as a need becomes clear, explain the barrier you are experiencing, and request a reasonable adjustment. Anderseed will discuss what can practically be provided for live sessions, recordings, documents, communication, or task submission.
What should I do if I have a technical access problem?
Report the issue promptly with enough information to identify the problem, while avoiding passwords or sensitive payment details. Anderseed will help with programme access it controls, but learners remain responsible for a suitable device, internet connection, email access, and any third-party account required for participation.
How can I ask a question or make a complaint?
Use the Contact Us section or email Anderseed with your name, the programme or service involved, and a clear description of the question or concern. Complaints will be reviewed fairly, with relevant records and programme terms considered, and privacy concerns can also be raised through the contact route in the privacy notice.
